name: Skill / Competency Definition
purpose: Represent scheme-scoped Skill and Competency definitions, immutable scheme releases, composition and explicitly lossy mappings without owning person capability assertions, assessments, qualifications, credentials or role assignments.

owns: skill and competency concept identity qualified by scheme and release
language-tagged labels definitions and concept type
competency composition from knowledge skill and applied behaviour references
context applicability deprecation and successor lineage
version-pinned directional concept mappings with purpose strength and semantic loss
delegates: proficiency scale identity and level semantics to an identifier-unassigned Proficiency Scale candidate
person capability holdings to an identifier-unassigned Person Capability Assertion candidate
qualification definitions and awards to WM-PER-008
issued credential identity and validity to WM-XCT-017
position expectations and requirements to WM-ORG-004

relations.purpose: Allow assessment criteria and results to pin immutable skill or competency definitions.
Allow position requirements to pin immutable concept and scale versions without becoming person assertions.
Allow credential evidence to cite concepts while issuance and validity remain credential-owned.

operations.effect: Issue an immutable content-addressed concept-scheme release.
Deprecate a concept with successor guidance without rewriting prior references.
Issue a context-qualified composition of knowledge skill and behaviour references.
Issue a directional purpose-limited mapping with declared loss.
Issue a successor mapping while preserving the predecessor.

invariants: A definition is never a person holding or capability assertion.
Every concept identity is qualified by scheme and immutable release.
Skill and competency are distinct concept types rather than aliases.
Skill denotes an atomic ability; competency composes knowledge skill and applied behaviour in a context.
Language-tagged labels never replace stable concept identifiers.
Deprecated concepts remain resolvable and point to explicit successors when available.
A level value is meaningless without a pinned external scale version.
Mappings pin both source and target scheme releases.
Mappings are directional purpose-limited and declare semantic loss.
Equal labels or numerals never imply exact equivalence across schemes or scales.
Assessment results never mutate concept definitions.
Credential validity is not current competence.
Role expectation is not a person capability assertion.
Human competency and AI-agent instruction packages never share identity.
